title: Faking carnival parades; Dejan's last Jefferson City parade
summary: Russell tells of fake players with potatoes in bell horns. Dejan tells how he used a borrowed upright bass and paid a man to carry it through the last Jefferson City carnival parade before the war.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: I was just thinking about Jack Lane, they call him Poppa Lane, a real old-time white drummer. He's 88 now. Yeah, Poppa Lane, yeah. Yeah, yeah. People tell him something that he'd have several bands out. They say sometimes on a big day, like Carnival Day, they'd fill up bands and they couldn't, some of the guys couldn't play to put potatoes on them. So they wouldn't make any noise. They'd make them think they'd blow them and they'd act like they'd blow them.

Well, I had a bass player one carnival day. The last parade they had for the Jefferson City budget before they stopped having parades, no right, when the beginning of the war, they didn't have that other carnival. But that was the last parade. I had a band out there, I had eight pieces. The trumpet, the bass player, I had to have another band. I said, what if I don't go to another band? The people say, you know, I have all the bands, you know, cut the money. I don't really need somebody to make that money. This boy, he needed money. I said, can you borrow that upright bass in front of God? He said, yeah. He said, up front of you is that upright bass. He went and get that upright bass. I said, are you just walking holding? And he walked that whole parade. I paid him.
That's right. Did you ever hear about anybody putting the potato or something? No. I never saw that.
I never saw that. I never saw that. I never saw that. I never saw that. It might be the truth now.
